detail.longDescription: I am packaging pip v26.2.2 as an RPM (python311-pip) to be installed inside a custom, isolated prefix. The target build environment is a completely clean, offline Docker container that lacks a pre-installed system pip, external package index access, or pre-packaged PEP 517 build backends. Environment Reproducer (Dockerfile) To illustrate the exact constraints, here is a minimal reproduction of the clean Docker build environment: FROM rockylinux:9-minimal # Setup isolated custom Python 3.11 prefix and minimal build tools RUN microdnf install -y rpm-build rpmdevtools dnf-plugins-core \ python311 python311-devel python311-setuptools \ pyproject-rpm-macros python3-rpm-generators zip unzip && \ microdnf clean all WORKDIR /build The Problem & Reference Spec Discrepancies While older enterprise RPM specs for Python 3.11 python-pip relied on deprecated legacy setup.py build paths, modern versions have migrated strictly to PEP 517 compliance governed by pyproject.toml (utilizing flit_core as its build backend). When examining modern reference implementations—such as CentOS Stream's and AlmaLinux's python3.14-pip.spec on c10s —they leverage modern RPM macros (%pyproject_wheel, %pyproject_install, %pyproject_save_files). However, adopting these macros inside our strictly isolated offline container introduces a circular bootstrapping dependency: Modern build macros and frontends internally invoke pip or build tools (python3-build, python3-installer) to compile packages. Because our target custom prefix and buildroot lack a pre-installed system pip or package index access, standard macro execution fails. Our build constraints strictly limit us to using only python311-devel, python311-setuptools, pyproject-rpm-macros, python3-rpm-generators, and basic archiving utilities (zip/unzip). When attempting to build the pip wheel using: %{\__python3} -m flit_core.wheel --outdir dist It fails because flit_core is not present in the clean environment. However, my build constraints strictly limit me to using only python311-devel , python311-setuptools , pyproject-rpm-macros , python3-rpm-generators , and basic archiving utilities ( zip / unzip ). I cannot rely on a pre-existing host pip to install build-time dependencies. I've tried: Downloading flit_core as a secondary source ( Source1 ) : I successfully unpack flit_core alongside pip during %prep and export its src/ path to PYTHONPATH . Extracting wheels manually : I tried building flit_core locally into a staging folder and extracting its .whl archive via Python’s zipfile module to avoid calling pip install (since pip isn't installed yet). Given this strictly isolated offline container setup and the explicit set of available build dependencies, how can we properly bootstrap and orchestrate flit_core as a local build backend during the rpmbuild %build phase to successfully generate and install the pip wheel into our custom prefix, bridging the gap between legacy specs and modern PEP 517 macro workflows?
